clue.text: Fail to impress and leave university; have a taste for beer at the present time — wholly in the present

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the word for wholly goes within the word for the present

parts.note: to go down is to leave Oxford or Cambridge at the end of term or for good
to have a taste for something is to like it
ale is a kind of beer
AD, anno domini, marks the present era
a boon is a gift or blessing
wholly means all of it

explanation.surface: A student who leaves university to spend time drinking beer, living wholly for the present.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno domini) is the present era. The pieces split differently in the answer, so beer and the date fuse into LEAD. The semicolon and dash only divide the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something received with complete indifference or disapproval, like a heavy balloon that cannot rise.

clue.text: Leave, before Spring's surrounded the gold with green growth, for a job in the Commonwealth

indicators.note: before places the word for leave ahead of the rest

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: something surrounded is enclosed, so the season word wraps around the gold and the colour
growth suggests the letters of the colour word develop into a new shape

parts.note: vernal means belonging to the spring
OR is gold in heraldry
the five letters of green rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone leaves before spring to take up a Commonwealth post, the scene full of gold and green.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry. Spring's must become the adjective for the season, not a noun, before it can surround anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A Governor-General represents the monarch in a Commonwealth realm such as Canada or Australia, so it is a post there.

clue.text: Beetle in charge of architectural style

parts.note: the dor is a dung beetle
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A beetle has been put in charge of the building's design.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, with plain capitals on its columns.

clue.text: Aboriginal stick for testing long-range weapons

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a throwing stick used by Aboriginal Australians to launch spears
second meaning: the South Australian rocket and missile test range

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a place, the Australian range named after the throwing stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a traditional spear-thrower and the Australian desert site where rockets and missiles were tested.

clue.text: Spartan in the use of words (US city section)

definitions.text: Spartan in the use of words

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a conic is a section of a cone, such as an ellipse

explanation.surface: A note on sparse speech, with a bracketed reference to part of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Spartans came from Laconia and were famed for terse replies, so the definition is doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A laconic speaker uses very few words, the brevity the Spartans of Laconia were proverbial for.

clue.text: King has queen to boss, being usually on hand

definitions.note: a riddling definition: the word usually comes after hand, as in handkerchief

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a chief is a boss

explanation.surface: A king has a queen to order him about.
explanation.walkthrough: On hand is read literally: the word is usually found with hand in front of it, making handkerchief.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerchief is a cloth square, and it is most often met joined to hand as the pocket handkerchief.

clue.text: One acquires a following, holding the note in spite of oneself

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the word for a following encloses the other letters

parts.note: a means one
to gain is to acquire
a train is a following or retinue
taken as written
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone gains followers while holding a note in a song they would rather not sing.
explanation.walkthrough: A following here is a retinue, the people who follow someone, not the act of following.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something against the grain means acting contrary to one's natural inclination, reluctantly.

clue.text: Familiar incompetent 8 near 14

definitions.note: a riddling definition: a town near the answer to 14

parts.note: old as in an old friend, a familiar one
8 is player, and an incompetent player is a ham

explanation.surface: A well-known bad actor working close to another place.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is MANCHESTER (the ship canal clue) and 8 is PLAYER. A ham is an overacting performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a Lancashire mill town a few miles north-east of Manchester city centre.

clue.text: Formerly at cricket, a professional musician?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: until 1962 English cricket split paid ... from amateur Gentlemen
second meaning: someone who plays an instrument

explanation.walkthrough: English cricket long held an annual Gentlemen v Players match between amateurs and paid professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word named a paid cricketer in the old class division and also anyone performing on an instrument.

clue.text: 54, the golden number for port

parts.note: LIV is 54 in Roman numerals
OR is gold in heraldry
NO is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Fifty-four is the golden number that unlocks a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The golden number is a real term in calendar reckoning, which makes the phrase look like one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Livorno, once called Leghorn in English, is a major Tuscan port on the Ligurian Sea.

clue.text: Dock — to prevent wagging?

definitions.note: a riddling definition read as cur tail
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a dog's tail, docked so it cannot wag

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading: a cur is a dog, and its tail is what wags.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to shorten or cut back, the same sense as docking an animal's tail or someone's pay.

clue.text: Goddess wholly belonging to labouring man

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
clean means completely, as in clean forgot

explanation.surface: A goddess entirely the property of a working man.
explanation.walkthrough: The labouring man is Heracles, famed for his twelve labours; Hera was his persecutor, which gives the surface an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraclean is the adjective for Heracles, the hero who performed twelve labours, so it means relating to him.

clue.text: Defence secretary holds French soldier and doctor after union
See 12
A navigable waterway, the English Channel (the Paris clan's version)

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so these letters are put in another order

parts.note: the French call the English Channel La Manche
all thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The English Channel as a Parisian family would name it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Paris and the bracket suggest a French translation, which is half right: only the Channel is translated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester Ship Canal links Manchester to the Mersey estuary and carries seagoing ships, so it is navigable.

clue.text: A small boy's acknowledgment of literary fragments

parts.note: an is the form of a before a vowel
Alec is a short form of Alexander, a boy's name
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A little boy says thank you for some scraps of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Small means the name is a shortened form, not that the boy is little.
explanation.definitionFit: Analecta are collected extracts or passages from writers, as in the Analects of Confucius.

clue.text: Fish about to drink a river — caveat emptor!

definitions.note: a warning phrase standing for the thing it warns about

indicators.note: about means around, so the fish surrounds what follows

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
gin is a drink
taken as written
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A fish swimming about as if to drink the river, with a warning to buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Latin warning itself, let the buyer beware, standing for the bad bargain it warns against.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying a pig in a poke is buying something unseen, exactly the risk that caveat emptor, let the buyer beware, warns of.

clue.text: Wrinkle sounds genuine

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by what is heard when the word for genuine is spoken

parts.note: pukka, from Hindi, means genuine or first-class

explanation.surface: A wrinkle that seems authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair match in a British accent that drops the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A pucker is a small fold or crease, so as a noun or verb it means a wrinkle.

clue.text: Saw expert cleric coming up second

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
B is second in grading

explanation.surface: An expert watched a clergyman arrive in second place.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw looks like the past of see; here it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, so a proverb is one.

clue.text: Expert on everything orders "walk on left"

indicators.note: orders here means arranges, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A self-styled expert issues an instruction to walk on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Orders looks like the giving of commands, with the quoted words as the command.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a person who behaves as if they know everything, an ironic self-proclaimed expert.

clue.text: See 14
Gates? Devastating 8

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes with Gates, as in the Pearly Gates

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: 8 is the answer to 8-down

explanation.surface: Gates, perhaps a sports star, as a devastating performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is PLAYER, whose letters are rearranged. The question mark shows the definition is an example of usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pearly Gates are the traditional entrance to heaven, so the adjective is the one that describes those gates.

clue.text: See 14
I am Pooh, sadly, swallowing silver and eating raw meat

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order
swallowing means taking inside, so the jumbled letters enclose the metal

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Winnie the Pooh confesses to swallowing silver and eating raw meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ag for silver comes from its Latin name argentum. The surface makes Pooh the eater; really his words are just letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Omophagia comes from Greek for raw and eating, the practice of eating uncooked flesh.

clue.text: Brother saying nothing to upset the chat show queen

indicators.note: in a down entry to upset something is to turn it upside down, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey is the famous American talk show host

explanation.surface: A brother keeps quiet so as not to annoy a television talk show host.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo was the Marx brother whose stage character never spoke, honking a horn instead.

clue.text: Trouble for the listener: each are at fault

indicators.note: at fault means in error, so the letters are wrongly placed and must be set right

parts.note: the seven letters as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that both parties are to blame, which a listener finds tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: Earache also means being nagged at length, which the scolding surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is pain in the ear, literally a problem for whoever is listening, and slang for a telling-off.

clue.text: Expose armour — it needs a sticker

parts.note: to air something is to expose it
mail is chain armour

explanation.surface: Laying bare a suit of armour, which turns out to need a label.
explanation.walkthrough: The sticker is the blue airmail label, or a stamp, on an overseas letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail letters carry a special label and postage stamps, both stuck on, before they can fly abroad.

clue.text: See 1
